description: Trend data sources for the Signal vs Noise Framework. Levels follow the Strong/Moderate/Weak signal tables; 'primary' sources are regulators, standards bodies, platform documentation, and filings (preferred for key claims per Web Search Safety).

sources.source: Regulators, standards bodies (ISO, W3C, IEEE), government filings
sources.what_to_track: New rules, comment periods, effective dates, certification requirements

sources.source: API/OS/cloud vendor release notes and changelogs
sources.what_to_track: New capabilities, deprecations, pricing changes, roadmap items

sources.source: SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, S-1), company annual reports
sources.what_to_track: Revenue mix, R&D direction, stated strategy, risk factors

sources.source: PitchBook, Crunchbase, CB Insights, quarterly VC activity reports
sources.what_to_track: Deal counts and dollar volume by category, round sizes, valuation step-ups
Acquisition targets and prices, strategic signals in acquirer messaging

sources.source: LinkedIn jobs, Indeed, company career pages
sources.what_to_track: Posting counts by role/technology, new role titles, geographic spread
Growth rate of key repos, contributor diversity, issue velocity

sources.source: Gartner, Forrester, IDC reports and vendor reference customers
sources.what_to_track: Magic Quadrant/Forrester Wave placements, enterprise case studies, TCO claims

sources.source: KubeCon, AWS re:Invent, WWDC, industry conference agendas
sources.what_to_track: New track names, talk density by topic, sponsor messaging

sources.source: Algolia Hacker News search, HN front page
sources.what_to_track: Mention frequency, comment sentiment, show-HN launches
Subscriber growth, post volume, recurring question topics

sources.source: Key voices on X/Twitter, LinkedIn, technical newsletters
sources.what_to_track: Which voices adopt, endorsement frequency, follow-up usage
Launch counts by category, upvote velocity, comment quality

sources.source: Blog post frequency, SEO content by topic
sources.what_to_track: New content velocity, content quality, author credibility
Mention frequency, which shows, follow-up episodes
Article frequency and framing; treat as lagging attention, not adoption
